name: Luxembourgish Judd mat Gaardebounen
description: Judd mat Gaardebounen, Luxembourg's national dish, is genuinely two separate components served together, not one combined stew - real smoked pork is soaked overnight to draw out excess salt before simmering with aromatics, while the broad beans are cooked entirely separately in their own real butter-flour roux enriched with white wine and cream.

ingredients_full.note: standing in for smoked pork collar

ingredients.note: standing in for smoked pork collar

steps_detailed: Simmer the pork with the carrot, leek, onion, and bay leaf in enough water to cover, 45-50 minutes.
Separately, simmer the fava beans in a little water 8-10 minutes until tender, then drain.
Melt the butter, whisk in the flour, cook 1 minute, then add the wine and cream, and simmer 3-4 minutes into a smooth sauce.
Fold the beans into the sauce.
Slice the pork and serve alongside the creamy beans as two distinct components on the same plate.

name: Luxembourgish Gromperekichelcher
description: Gromperekichelcher, crispy grated potato fritters, are a beloved Luxembourgish street food, real technique squeezing the grated potato well and seasoning generously with nutmeg alongside onion and parsley.

ingredients_full.note: tbsp, chopped, standing in for parsley

ingredients.note: tbsp, chopped, standing in for parsley

steps_detailed: Squeeze the grated potato and onion well to remove excess liquid.
Mix with the parsley, egg, flour, and nutmeg.
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil and fry, flattening slightly, 3-4 minutes per side, until deeply golden and crisp.

name: Luxembourgish Bouneschlupp (Green Bean Soup)
description: Bouneschlupp, a real green bean and bacon soup with potato, is a genuine Luxembourgish comfort staple, real technique cooking the bacon first to render its fat as the flavor base.
steps_detailed: Cook the bacon and onion together, 4-5 minutes.
Add the potato and 2 cups water, and simmer 12-15 minutes.
Add the green beans and simmer 12-15 minutes more until everything is tender.

name: Luxembourgish Quetschentaart (Plum Tart)
description: Quetschentaart, a real open-faced plum tart, is a beloved Luxembourgish autumn dessert, real technique arranging the plum halves cut-side up so their juices concentrate as they bake rather than soaking into the crust.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Peaches, canned, extra light syrup, solids and liquids (Includes foods for USDA's Food Distribution Program)

steps_detailed: Mix the flour, butter, and half the sugar into a firm dough, and press into a small tart pan.
Arrange the fruit cut-side up over the dough, and sprinkle with the remaining sugar and cinnamon.
Bake at 375F (190C) for 30-35 minutes until the crust is golden and the fruit has caramelized.

name: Luxembourgish Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish rubbed with butter and herbs, reflecting Luxembourg's real Moselle River fishing tradition.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the melted butter and dill.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

name: Luxembourgish Roasted Almonds
description: A simple roasted almond snack, common across Luxembourg.

Add the carrot, potato, and tomatoes, and simmer 30-35 minutes until tender.
